idiom_name: object declaration NoOp + nullable types with ?. / ?:
implementation_notes: Kotlin's type system makes absence explicit (Listener?), and ?., ?: and orEmpty() handle the nullable path in a single expression, so the classic null-subclass structure is rarely needed. When the collaborator must be non-null - a field that is always called - the pattern costs one line: object NoOpListener : Listener { override fun onEvent(id: Int) = Unit }, a lazily initialised singleton with no allocation; for a single-method interface, fun interface plus a lambda (Listener { }) is even shorter. Prefer the nullable type when the caller must know that nothing is listening; prefer the null object when it must not.
pitfalls: ?. and !! can hide the absence the type system just made explicit: listener?.onEvent(id) silently skips every event, and !! throws where the null object was the point - decide per call site which behaviour is intended.

lateinit and Java platform types break the guarantee: a lateinit var can still be uninitialised and a Java getter returns a platform type the compiler cannot check, so install the null object at construction.
Object declarations initialise lazily on first access; they are still singletons, but do not give a null object mutable state that other threads can observe.
